views.name: classroom_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  room_number,
  capacity
FROM classroom

params.description: Provides one row per classroom (building + room_number) with its seating capacity.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve capacity for a specific classroom given building and room_number. | List all classrooms and their capacities in a building or across buildings. | Join classroom-level capacity information into higher-level queries (e.g., building summaries) while preserving one-row-per-classroom semantics. | Compose into aggregations (e.g., total capacity per building) by aggregating the capacity column.
params.output_schema: building: identifier/name of the building that contains the classroom; derived directly from classroom.building | room_number: identifier/number of the room within the building; derived directly from classroom.room_number | capacity: seating capacity (number of seats) for that classroom; derived directly from classroom.capacity
params.metric: capacity = classroom.capacity (base non-aggregated numeric attribute representing seats in the room)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to building-level one-row-per-building views or tables on building — safe because this view is at most one row per (building, room_number) and joining to one-row-per-building will not duplicate classroom rows' measures when you intend to preserve classroom granularity. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a rooms-dimension that is also one-row-per-(building,room_number) on (building, room_number) — safe because keys match one-to-one and will not multiply measures. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT naively join to any one-to-many table/view (for example, a bookings, classes_scheduled, or equipment table that can have multiple rows per classroom) without re-aggregation, because such joins will duplicate classroom.capacity for each matching child row and thus overcount capacity-based measures. | safe-composition pattern for one-to-many children: to incorporate information from a one-to-many child (e.g., bookings), first aggregate the child by (building, room_number) (for example COUNT(*) AS booking_count) and then join that aggregated result to classroom_rows on (building, room_number). This preserves correct counts and avoids multiplying classroom.capacity. | aggregation guidance: to compute building-level totals (e.g., total capacity per building), aggregate capacity using SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building on this view; do not SUM after joining to an unaggregated many-side table unless that many-side has been aggregated or de-duplicated.

views.name: classroom_capacity_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  room_number,
  CAST(capacity AS INTEGER) AS capacity_int
FROM
  classroom_rows

params.description: Provides one row per classroom (building + room_number) with the room capacity as an integer.
params.when_to_use: Get the integer seating capacity for a specific classroom (building + room_number). | Filter or list classrooms by capacity thresholds (e.g., capacity >= N). | Compose into room-level reports that need a stable, integer capacity measure. | Join with schedules or bookings aggregated at the classroom level (building + room_number) to compute utilization.
params.output_schema: building: building identifier for the classroom — derived directly from base column classroom_rows.building | room_number: room identifier within the building — derived directly from base column classroom_rows.room_number | capacity_int: classroom capacity converted to integer — derived from base column classroom_rows.capacity via CAST(capacity AS INTEGER)
params.metric: capacity_int = CAST(classroom_rows.capacity AS INTEGER)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a building-level dimension/view on building — safe because this view is one-row-per (building, room_number); joining on building alone will not duplicate this view's measures as long as the building dimension is one-row-per building. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a room-dimension/view on (building, room_number) — safe because both sides should be one-row-per room; this preserves capacity_int without duplication. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many event/booking/schedule tables (e.g., bookings with many rows per room) without re-aggregating the downstream table first — doing so will multiply the room-level capacity_int per matching booking row and inflate any sums of capacity_int. | If you need aggregated metrics that combine capacity_int with many-row tables, either (a) aggregate the many-row table to the same grain (building, room_number) before joining, or (b) join then re-aggregate and compute measures using appropriate DISTINCT/SAFE aggregations to avoid duplication.

views.name: sections_with_classroom
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  section.course_id AS course_id,
  section.sec_id AS sec_id,
  section.semester AS semester,
  section.year AS year,
  section.building AS building,
  section.room_number AS room_number
FROM section
JOIN classroom_rows
  ON section.building = classroom_rows.building
  AND section.room_number = classroom_rows.room_number

params.description: Rows of course sections that have a matching classroom record (section rows enriched with verified classroom building and room_number).
params.when_to_use: Find sections and their classroom location for a given semester/year. | Filter or list course sections that are present in the classroom inventory (i.e., have a matching building and room). | As a base (grain: course_id, sec_id, semester, year) to join classroom-level attributes (capacity, features) without duplicating section rows.
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the course this section belongs to — derived from base table column section.course_id | sec_id: section identifier within the course — derived from base table column section.sec_id | semester: academic term label for the section (e.g., 'Fall') — derived from base table column section.semester | year: academic year for the section — derived from base table column section.year | building: building code/name where the section is scheduled — derived from base table column section.building (filtered to rows that match classroom_rows) | room_number: room number where the section is scheduled — derived from base table column section.room_number (filtered to rows that match classroom_rows)
params.grounded_columns: section.course_id | section.sec_id | section.semester | section.year | section.building | section.room_number | classroom_rows.building | classroom_rows.room_number
params.metric: This view exposes no new aggregated metrics. All output columns are passthrough (section.*) with an inner-join filter to classroom_rows. Example derived indicator (not present as a column): section_has_classroom = 1 for every row in this view (i.e., presence flag implied by the inner join).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_capacity_projection on (building, room_number) — safe because classroom_capacity_projection is a classroom-level projection (one row per building+room_number) so joining will not duplicate this view's one-row-per-(course_id,sec_id,semester,year) rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_rows on (building, room_number) — safe for the same reason (classroom_rows is keyed by building+room_number), and the original view already required a matching classroom_rows row, so this is referentially one-to-one from the section row to the classroom row. | UNSAFE join warning: do NOT join directly to tables that are one-to-many relative to a section (for example, a hypothetical meeting_times or enrollments table keyed at a finer grain than course_id+sec_id+semester+year) without first aggregating or deduplicating those tables to the section grain. Such joins would multiply rows and thus duplicate any implied per-section measures (e.g., the implicit section_has_classroom flag). | UNSAFE join warning: do NOT join to a schedule_events or student_attendance table at the event/student level without aggregation to course_id+sec_id+semester+year first — otherwise counts or sums will be inflated. | If you need aggregated metrics per section (e.g., student_count, total_hours), compute those metrics from their source tables grouped to (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) and then join the aggregated result to this view on (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) to preserve correctness.

params.metric: capacity = classroom.capacity  -- not an aggregate; a base attribute (per-row measure) representing number of seats in the classroom
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional/look-up views that are one-row-per-building (e.g., building-level views) on building — safe because classroom_rows_3 is one-row-per(building,room_number) and joining to a one-row-per-building dimension does NOT duplicate classroom_rows_3 rows | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per(classroom) view (e.g., sibling view classroom_rows or classroom_capacity_projection) on (building, room_number) — safe because both sides are at the same grain (building, room_number) so measures like capacity are not duplicated | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example sections_with_classroom or any sections/events table that has multiple rows per classroom) without re-aggregation — such joins will duplicate capacity values because sections_with_classroom contains multiple section rows per (building, room_number); to combine total seats available per classroom with sections, first aggregate the one-to-many side (e.g., count sections per classroom or sum attendance) and then join back on (building, room_number) | when composing metrics across grains: if you need an aggregate of capacity after joining to a detail table (e.g., total capacity across rooms that have sections), either (a) group by classroom_rows_3.building, classroom_rows_3.room_number and apply aggregates on capacity before joining to detail; or (b) join detail -> aggregate(detail) per classroom -> then join the aggregated detail to classroom_rows_3 on (building, room_number). This prevents multiplication of capacity by multiple detail rows. | keys to join on: use the composite key (building, room_number) to match classrooms deterministically; do not rely on building alone unless intentionally aggregating across rooms

views.name: classrooms_by_building_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  COUNT(room_number) AS classroom_count
FROM classroom
GROUP BY building

params.description: Counts of classrooms per building (one row per building with the number of rooms in that building).
params.when_to_use: Report total number of classrooms grouped by building. | Compose higher-level metrics that need classroom counts per building (e.g., capacity per building when joined to capacity projections). | Filter or join to building-level analyses where classroom counts are required as an aggregated attribute.
params.output_schema: building: identifier/name of the building as provided by classroom.building (source column: classroom.building) | classroom_count: number of classroom rows that share the building (derived metric: COUNT(room_number) over rows in classroom grouped by building; source column used: classroom.room_number)
params.metric: classroom_count = COUNT(classroom.room_number) GROUP BY classroom.building
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to building-level dimensions or views (e.g., a buildings dimension view keyed by building) on classroom.building — safe because this view has exactly one row per building, so joining to another one-row-per-building view preserves one row per building and does NOT duplicate classroom_count. | You can safely join to classroom_capacity_projection (NORM) if that view is also one-row-per-building and keyed by classroom.building; the classroom_count measure will not be duplicated in that case. | Do NOT join directly to classroom_rows (SEL) or any other one-to-many table/view keyed to building (for example, a raw classroom_rows or sections_with_classroom that has multiple rows per building) without first aggregating that one-to-many side to one row per building. Joining this AGG view to a many-rows-per-building table will multiply classroom_count and produce incorrect totals unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you need to combine classroom_count with metrics at the classroom or section grain (e.g., join to sections_with_classroom which lists multiple sections per classroom), either: (a) aggregate that detail-side up to building before joining, or (b) join first and then compute distinct/count aggregations from the joined result, ensuring you do not double-count. | Joining to classroom_rows_3 (NORM) is only safe if classroom_rows_3 is guaranteed to be one-row-per-building; otherwise re-aggregate classroom_rows_3 to building grain before joining. | In planner terms: treat this view as a dimension-like, one-row-per-building relation. Any join where the other side is one-row-per-building on the same key preserves measures; any join to a many-per-building side requires aggregation (SUM, COUNT DISTINCT as appropriate) to avoid multiplicative duplication of classroom_count.

Directly joining a one-to-many relation will multiply section rows and thus multiply any derived counts/metrics. | when joining to sibling view sections_with_classroom (JOIN) or other section-level views that share the same grain (course_id, sec_id, semester, year), ensure the join keys are exactly (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) and that the sibling view is also one-row-per-section; this will not duplicate rows. If the sibling view has a different grain (e.g., multiple rows per section), aggregate it to the section grain first. | if you need to produce section-level aggregates after joining to a many-side, perform grouping/aggregation back to (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) so measures remain correct. | explicit join key examples (SAFE):

views.name: department_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name AS dept_name,
  building AS building,
  budget AS budget
FROM department

params.description: Provides one-row-per-department basic attributes (department name, building, budget).
params.when_to_use: Look up a department's building or budget given dept_name | Filter or join departments as a dimensional table when computing aggregates at the department level | Compose into reports that need department-level attributes (e.g., attach department budget to aggregated section or classroom metrics) after ensuring join cardinality is respected
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (derived from department.dept_name) | building: building where the department is located (derived from department.building) | budget: department budget amount (derived from department.budget)
params.metric: dept_name = department.dept_name | building = department.building | budget = department.budget
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-department on department.dept_name — e.g., join to a department-level view keyed by dept_name — safe because department_basic itself is one-row-per-dept_name, so measures (budget) will not be duplicated. | do NOT join department_basic directly to one-to-many tables or views (for example, sections_with_classroom, classroom_rows, classrooms_by_building_cohort, sections_with_classroom_5) on dept_name without aggregation on the one-to-many side first — those joins will multiply department_basic rows and duplicate the budget value unless you aggregate the many-side metrics (SUM, COUNT, AVG as appropriate) grouped by dept_name before joining. | If you need department-level totals combined with many-side details, either: (a) aggregate the many-side to dept_name first (e.g., SELECT dept_name, SUM(...) FROM sections_with_classroom GROUP BY dept_name) then join to department_basic, or (b) join and then re-aggregate grouping by department_basic.dept_name to collapse duplicates. | Joining to sibling normalized/one-row-per-department views (like other NORM views keyed by dept_name) is safe on dept_name because both sides are one-row-per-department. | Joining on keys other than dept_name: verify the other view/table is one-row-per-that-key. For example, joining department_basic.building to a one-row-per-building view keyed by building is safe; joining to classroom_rows (which is one-to-many by building) is not safe without prior aggregation.

views.name: department_budget_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name,
  building,
  budget,
  AVG(budget) OVER () AS avg_budget_overall
FROM
  department

params.description: Per-department budget and building with the overall average budget repeated for each department row.
params.when_to_use: Report departmental budget alongside the overall average budget across all departments. | Compose reports that compare each department's budget to the university-wide average budget. | Filter or group departments by building while showing each department's budget and the global average for context. | Serve as a base for further aggregation at the department level (e.g., counts of departments by building with budget statistics).
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (sourced from department.dept_name) | building: department building (sourced from department.building) | budget: department budget (sourced from department.budget) | avg_budget_overall: overall average of department.budget across all department rows (window AVG(budget) OVER ())
params.metric: avg_budget_overall = AVG(department.budget) OVER ()  -- windowed global average of the department.budget column | budget = department.budget  -- base numeric column, not an aggregate in this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-department (for example, a 'department_basic' normalized view keyed by department.dept_name if that view is one-row-per-department) on department.dept_name — safe because department_budget_stats is one-row-per-dept_name and joining to another one-row-per-department relation preserves row cardinality so budgets and the avg_budget_overall are not duplicated. | do NOT join department_budget_stats directly to tables or views that are one-to-many relative to department (for example: sections, classrooms if multiple classrooms map to a department, or any sections_with_classroom / sections_with_classroom_5 if they contain multiple section rows per department) without first aggregating the many-side back to department level. Such joins would duplicate department_budget_stats rows and therefore duplicate budget and the repeated avg_budget_overall values, inflating sums or counts. | If you need to combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., classroom_rows, sections_with_classroom), options are: (a) pre-aggregate the child to one row per department (e.g., SUM(seats) BY dept_name) and then join on dept_name; or (b) join and then re-aggregate at the department grain (e.g., GROUP BY dept_name with appropriate aggregates for measures). Both ensure measures in this view are not multiplied. | Safe join keys: department.dept_name is the intended key. Avoid joining on non-unique department attributes (e.g., building alone) unless you intend to create a many-to-many expansion and handle re-aggregation. | Because avg_budget_overall is a windowed global measure repeated on every row, it remains valid after row-level filtering that does not change the underlying department table used to compute the window. If you filter this view before computing the average in another context, be aware the stored avg_budget_overall here reflects the average over the full department table as defined in the view SQL, not the filtered subset.

views.name: department_with_courses_count
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  d.budget,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS course_count
FROM department d
LEFT JOIN course c
  ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  d.budget

params.description: For each department (dept_name, building, budget) return the number of courses offered by that department.
params.when_to_use: Count courses per department (reporting or dashboards showing course counts by department). | As a building block for queries that need department-level course volume combined with other department attributes (e.g., budget, building). | To filter or rank departments by how many courses they offer (top-N departments by course_count). | To join department-level course counts into higher-level department analytics (budget vs. course count comparisons).
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (derived from base table department.dept_name) | building: department building/location (derived from base table department.building) | budget: department budget (derived from base table department.budget) | course_count: number of courses associated with the department (derived metric COUNT(course.course_id) over left-joined course rows grouped by department)
params.metric: course_count = COUNT(course.course_id) grouped by department.dept_name, department.building, department.budget  -- counts course rows linked to the department; uses a LEFT JOIN so departments with zero courses produce course_count = 0
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_basic (or any view that is one-row-per-department) on department.dept_name — safe because department_with_courses_count is one-row-per-department (grain = dept_name, building, budget) so measures are not duplicated when combined with another one-row-per-department relation. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_budget_stats on department.dept_name — safe if department_budget_stats is aggregated at department level (one row per dept_name); this preserves course_count without duplication. | do NOT join directly to course (or any other one-to-many detail table such as sections) without re-aggregating, because joining a department-level aggregated view to multiple course/section rows will multiply course_count and other department-level measures. If you must combine with course-level detail, either: |   - join department_with_courses_count to course on dept_name and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., SUM(course_count) is not meaningful; instead recompute counts from course rows), or |   - join department_with_courses_count to a deduplicated department dimension (one row per dept_name) or to an aggregated view that is one-row-per-department. | do NOT join to sections_with_classroom or sections_with_classroom_5 (both are likely one-to-many to department through course/section) without first aggregating those section-level views to department granularity, because each section row would duplicate the department's course_count. | safe-to-join examples: |   - join to department_basic on department.dept_name (one-row-per-department) — preserves course_count |   - join to department_budget_stats on department.dept_name (if that view is aggregated to department) — preserves course_count | unsafe-to-join examples (unless re-aggregated): |   - join to course on dept_name (many courses per department) — will multiply department rows and duplicate course_count |   - join to sections_with_classroom or sections_with_classroom_5 on dept_name (sections are many per department) — will multiply this view's rows/measures | notes on nulls and zero counts: because the SQL uses LEFT JOIN from department to course and COUNT(course.course_id), departments with no matching course rows will yield course_count = 0 (COUNT of non-null course_id returns 0).

views.description: For each department (dept_name, building, budget) return the number of courses offered by that department.

views.name: classroom_capacity_by_building

SELECT

  AVG(classroom.capacity) AS avg_classroom_capacity,
  COUNT(classroom.room_number) AS num_classrooms
FROM classroom
WHERE classroom.capacity IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY classroom.building

params.description: Per-building aggregate of classroom counts and average classroom capacity.
params.when_to_use: Report average classroom capacity and number of classrooms per building. | As a building-level input when computing capacity-based metrics (e.g., average capacity across selected buildings). | When joining building-level classroom capacity metrics to other building/dimension tables to enrich reports or dashboards. | As a pre-aggregated source to join with building-level cohorts or department summaries (but avoid joining to row-level classroom or section data without re-aggregation).
params.output_schema: building: the building identifier/name sourced from classroom.building | avg_classroom_capacity: the average of classroom.capacity across classrooms in the building; derived from AVG(classroom.capacity) | num_classrooms: the count of distinct classroom room_number values in the building as counted in this view; derived from COUNT(classroom.room_number)
params.metric: avg_classroom_capacity = AVG(classroom.capacity)  -- average of non-NULL classroom.capacity for rows grouped by classroom.building | num_classrooms = COUNT(classroom.room_number)    -- count of classroom.room_number values (rows) per classroom.building; the underlying query filters out rows where classroom.capacity IS NULL before counting
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to building-level dimensions or aggregates (e.g., classrooms_by_building_cohort (AGG) or any building-level selector) on classroom.building — safe because this view is one row per building, so building-level joins do not duplicate the measures. | Do NOT join directly to classroom_rows (SEL) or classroom_rows_3 (NORM) or any other one-to-many classroom/section row-level tables (e.g., sections_with_classroom, sections_with_classroom_5) without re-aggregating those tables to building-level first, because those row-level joins would multiply this view's rows and thereby incorrectly inflate avg_classroom_capacity and num_classrooms. | If you need to combine with section-level data, first aggregate the section-level data to building (e.g., count sections per building) and then join on building to preserve correct aggregated semantics. | When joining to department or instructor-level views (e.g., department_rows, department_with_courses_count, instructor_by_department), ensure there is a stable one-row-per-building key relationship (if department is mapped to building); if the join is one-to-many (a building hosting multiple departments or a department present in multiple buildings), re-aggregate appropriately on the department side or join the department -> building mapping at the correct grain to avoid duplicating measures. | If you need to compute weighted averages across buildings (for example, a system-wide average classroom capacity), use num_classrooms as the weight: system_avg = SUM(avg_classroom_capacity * num_classrooms) / SUM(num_classrooms) — do not take a simple average of avg_classroom_capacity across buildings unless each building should be weighted equally.

views.description: Per-building aggregate of classroom counts and average classroom capacity.

Such joins would multiply dept_budget_avg and num_departments unless you re-aggregate after the join or join on suitably reduced/aggregated keys. | safe composition pattern when joining to one-to-many: if you must join to a one-to-many detail (e.g., sections) to compute a ratio, first aggregate the detail to one row per building (e.g., total_students_by_building) and then join that aggregated result to avg_department_budget_by_building on building. | re-aggregation rule: if you join avg_department_budget_by_building to a lower-grain table and want to preserve correct building-level measures, perform the join and then GROUP BY avg_department_budget_by_building.building and use aggregate functions (e.g., AVG(MAX(dept_budget_avg)) is not appropriate); instead, use constructs that treat dept_budget_avg and num_departments as measures that should be summarized correctly (for example, compute weighted averages by reusing num_departments as weight: overall_budget_avg = SUM(dept_budget_avg * num_departments) / SUM(num_departments)). | note on NULL filtering: the view excludes department rows where budget IS NULL; when composing with other sources that include departments with NULL budget, be aware that num_departments and dept_budget_avg reflect only departments with non-null budgets.

views.name: classroom_capacity_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,

FROM classroom

params.description: Provides the capacity of each classroom at the grain of building + room_number.
params.when_to_use: Lookup the seating capacity for a specific classroom (by building and room_number). | Filter or join classroom capacity information into schedules, sections, or room-utilization queries. | Compose higher-level aggregates of classroom capacity (e.g., total capacity per building) by aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: building: building identifier for the classroom. Derived directly from base table column classroom.building. | room_number: room identifier within the building. Derived directly from base table column classroom.room_number. | capacity: seating capacity (numeric) of the classroom. Derived directly from base table column classroom.capacity.
params.metric: capacity = classroom.capacity  -- a base attribute (not an aggregate) representing the seating capacity for the classroom at the building+room_number grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookup tables keyed 1:1 on (building, room_number) — e.g., join to classroom_rows or classroom_rows_3 on (building, room_number) — safe because classroom_capacity_cohort is one row per (building, room_number) so joining 1:1 does not duplicate capacity values. | It is safe to aggregate this view upward (for example SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building) to produce building-level capacity metrics; do not aggregate and then join back to a many-row fact without aligning grain. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views that have multiple rows per (building, room_number) (for example sections_with_classroom or sections_with_classroom_5) without re-aggregation or distincting, because those joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate the capacity measure. If you need total capacity alongside per-section rows, either: |   - pre-aggregate classroom_capacity_cohort to the desired grain (e.g., building) and join on building, or |   - join sections_with_classroom to a single-row-per-classroom result (this view) but ensure the join key is exactly (building, room_number) and that sections_with_classroom rows are understood to be many per classroom — in that case do not SUM(capacity) after the join without grouping by classroom identifiers to avoid double-counting. | When composing with sibling aggregate views (e.g., classrooms_by_building_cohort), prefer joining on building only if the sibling view is at building grain; avoid joining a classroom-level view to a classroom-level one-to-many expansion without re-aggregation. | Example safe patterns: |   - To get total capacity per building: SELECT building, SUM(capacity) FROM classroom_capacity_cohort GROUP BY building; |   - To attach capacity to a schedule row that references a single classroom: JOIN classroom_capacity_cohort ON schedule.building = classroom_capacity_cohort.building AND schedule.room_number = classroom_capacity_cohort.room_number (safe because join is to the single matching classroom row). | Example unsafe pattern: |   - SELECT s.section_id, c.capacity FROM sections_with_classroom s JOIN classroom_capacity_cohort c USING (building, room_number); then SUM(capacity) over sections will double-count if multiple sections map to the same classroom — re-aggregate or GROUP BY classroom identifiers before summing.

views.name: section_room_mapping
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  c.capacity
FROM
  sections_with_classroom s
LEFT JOIN

ON
  s.building = c.building
  AND s.room_number = c.room_number

params.description: Maps each section (course + sec_id in a semester/year) to the classroom assigned (building, room_number) and the classroom capacity when available.
params.when_to_use: Find which room a given section met in for a specific semester/year and the room's capacity if known. | Compose section-level reports that need classroom location and capacity (e.g., seat utilization = enrollment / capacity) while preserving section grain. | Filter or group sections by building, room_number, semester, or year. | Join to instructor, course, or department dimensions at the section grain to enrich section rows with classroom info.
params.output_schema: course_id: course identifier for the section — derived from sections_with_classroom.course_id | sec_id: section identifier within the course — derived from sections_with_classroom.sec_id | semester: academic term label for the section — derived from sections_with_classroom.semester | year: academic year for the section — derived from sections_with_classroom.year | building: building code/name where the section met — derived from sections_with_classroom.building | room_number: room identifier within the building where the section met — derived from sections_with_classroom.room_number | capacity: seating capacity of the classroom — derived from classroom_rows.capacity (nullable because LEFT JOIN may produce NULL when classroom not found)
params.grounded_columns: sections_with_classroom.course_id | sections_with_classroom.sec_id | sections_with_classroom.semester | sections_with_classroom.year | sections_with_classroom.building | sections_with_classroom.room_number | classroom_rows.capacity | classroom_rows.building | classroom_rows.room_number
params.metric: capacity = classroom_rows.capacity  -- directly projected; not an aggregate in this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a section-level or one-row-per-section view/table (for example, sections_with_classroom or another view aggregated to the same grain) on (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — safe because section_room_mapping is one-row-per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year), so joining on that key does not duplicate its rows or the capacity value. | Safe to join to instructor_by_department or department_rows (dimension/lookup tables) on their natural keys (e.g., department_id) only if those tables are one-row-per-dimension; they will not duplicate section_room_mapping rows because the join is many-sections-to-one-dimension. | Do NOT join naively to any table/view that is one-to-many from the section grain (for example, a view that lists multiple enrollments, multiple meeting times per section, or multiple classroom_history rows per section) without either: | - aggregating that one-to-many side to the section grain first (so the join keys remain one-to-one or many-to-one), or | - explicitly re-aggregating after the join to remove duplication. | Example problematic joins (will multiply rows/measures): | - joining to a hypothetical enrollments table that has one row per student enrollment for the same section (would duplicate capacity per student), | - joining to a classroom_rows_3 or classrooms_by_building_cohort if those sibling views are aggregations that produce multiple rows per building/room (verify their grain) — if they are one-row-per-(building,room) they are safe; if not, aggregate first. | If you need section-level metrics derived from capacity (e.g., seat_utilization = enrolled_count / capacity), compute enrolled_count at section grain first (aggregate enrollments to course_id, sec_id, semester, year), then join that result to section_room_mapping on (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) to avoid duplication.

views.description: Maps each section (course + sec_id in a semester/year) to the classroom assigned (building, room_number) and the classroom capacity when available.

Such a join would multiply the student rows and therefore duplicate any measures that are attached to this view. | If you need to bring in one-to-many data (enrollments, sections, scores) do it by either: 1) aggregating the many-side to one row per student.ID before joining (e.g., COUNT(enrollment_id) AS enroll_count grouped by student.ID), or 2) join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY student.ID after joining). | Examples of safe join keys in this database: join student_name_lookup.ID = sections_with_classroom.student_id (only if sections_with_classroom is known to be one-row-per-student; otherwise aggregate sections_with_classroom by student_id first). | Examples of unsafe joins without aggregation: joining directly to classroom_rows, sections_with_classroom, classroom_rows_3, sections_with_classroom_5, or other JOIN/AGG views that represent multiple rows per student (or multiple rows per ID) because those could multiply student_name_lookup rows/measures.

views.name: classroom_capacity_categories
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  'Small' AS size_category,
  0 AS min_capacity_inclusive,
  20 AS max_capacity_inclusive
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Medium' AS size_category,
  21 AS min_capacity_inclusive,
  50 AS max_capacity_inclusive
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Large' AS size_category,
  51 AS min_capacity_inclusive,
  200 AS max_capacity_inclusive
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Extra Large' AS size_category,
  201 AS min_capacity_inclusive,
  1000 AS max_capacity_inclusive

params.description: Provides a fixed lookup of classroom size categories and their inclusive minimum and maximum capacity bounds.
params.when_to_use: Classify a classroom or section into a size category based on its capacity (e.g., label a room with capacity=34 as 'Medium'). | Filter or bucket reports, cohorts, or aggregates by classroom size category. | Join size-category ranges into projections or planning queries that need bucket boundaries (e.g., capacity projection, utilization thresholds). | Drive UI dropdowns or validation rules that require canonical size-category boundaries.
params.output_schema: size_category: human-readable category name for capacity buckets (derived directly from the SELECT literal 'Small'|'Medium'|'Large'|'Extra Large' in this view) | min_capacity_inclusive: integer lower bound (inclusive) of the capacity range for this category (derived from the SELECT literal values 0, 21, 51, 201 in this view) | max_capacity_inclusive: integer upper bound (inclusive) of the capacity range for this category (derived from the SELECT literal values 20, 50, 200, 1000 in this view)
params.grounded_columns: This view is a reshaped constant set and does not reference any base table columns. The SQL supplies the three output columns as literals: size_category, min_capacity_inclusive, max_capacity_inclusive.
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All outputs are deterministic constants per size_category. | Usage pattern for deriving a metric externally: count_classrooms_in_category = COUNT(*) after joining/ filtering classrooms to this view by capacity BETWEEN min_capacity_inclusive AND max_capacity_inclusive
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join this view to classroom-level data (e.g., classrooms, classroom_rows, classroom_rows_3, classroom_capacity_projection) by applying a predicate that tests the classroom capacity against the category bounds (e.g., ON classroom.capacity BETWEEN classroom_capacity_categories.min_capacity_inclusive AND classroom_capacity_categories.max_capacity_inclusive). Safe because this view is one-row-per-size_category and the join is a many(classroom)-to-one(size_category) mapping — each classroom matches exactly one category, so aggregations over classrooms will not be duplicated when grouping by size_category. | You may also LEFT JOIN categories to an aggregated result keyed by size_category (for example, when you pre-aggregate classrooms by size_category). Doing so remains safe because the category side is one-row-per-size_category; it will not multiply the aggregated measures from the other side. | Do NOT perform a direct cross-join or an unconditional many-to-many join between this view and a one-to-many detail table (for example joining without a capacity predicate to a sections_with_classroom or sections table) because that would create a Cartesian-like expansion and multiply measures. Always join by evaluating capacity bounds or by joining on a precomputed size_category key present on the other table. | Examples of safe compositions: | - Safe: SELECT c.building, cat.size_category, COUNT(*) FROM classroom_rows AS c JOIN classroom_capacity_categories AS cat ON c.capacity BETWEEN cat.min_capacity_inclusive AND cat.max_capacity_inclusive GROUP BY c.building, cat.size_category | - Safe: LEFT JOIN categories to a summarized table that already has one row per size_category (no duplication): classrooms_by_building_cohort LEFT JOIN classroom_capacity_categories USING (size_category) — only safe if classrooms_by_building_cohort is guaranteed one-row-per-size_category. | Examples of unsafe compositions: | - Unsafe: JOIN classroom_capacity_categories to sections_with_classroom without using the capacity-range predicate or a precomputed size_category on sections_with_classroom — this may multiply rows and overcount measures. | - Unsafe: Cross joining this view to other multi-row tables (e.g., departments, sections) without a deterministic one-to-one or many-to-one predicate.

views.description: Provides a fixed lookup of classroom size categories and their inclusive minimum and maximum capacity bounds.

views.name: classroom_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom

params.description: Provides the capacity of each classroom at the grain of (building, room_number).
params.when_to_use: Look up the seating capacity for a specific classroom identified by building and room_number | Filter or group metrics by classroom location when building reports or aggregations are needed | Join classroom capacity onto other datasets keyed by (building, room_number) to enrich them with capacity before further aggregation
params.output_schema: building: building identifier/name, derived from classroom.building | room_number: room identifier within the building, derived from classroom.room_number | capacity: seating capacity (integer) of the classroom, derived from classroom.capacity
params.metric: capacity = classroom.capacity  -- identity projection (no aggregation) representing the room's capacity at the (building, room_number) grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key views/tables on (building, room_number) — e.g., a view that has one row per classroom (same keys) — safe because classroom_by_building is one-row-per-(building,room_number) so measures (capacity) will not be duplicated. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed only by building (or by building + room_number if that target is one-to-many) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate capacity values. For example, joining to a sections table that has multiple sections per classroom will produce multiple rows per classroom and thus over-count capacity unless you first aggregate sections (e.g., count sections per classroom) or aggregate capacity after the join. | If you need classroom capacity aggregated to a different grain (e.g., building-level total capacity), aggregate this view (SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building) rather than joining classroom_by_building to another many-row table and then aggregating, to avoid duplication. | Safe join example: JOIN classroom_by_building cb ON cb.building = classroom.building AND cb.room_number = classroom.room_number when enriching a single-row-per-classroom dataset. | Unsafe join example: JOIN classroom_by_building cb ON cb.building = dept.building when dept has many rows per building (this would replicate cb.capacity across dept rows); instead first aggregate cb to building-level or aggregate after joining with DISTINCT classrooms.

views.description: Provides the capacity of each classroom at the grain of (building, room_number).

views.name: advisor_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s_ID,
  i_ID
FROM
  advisor

params.description: List of advisor relationships as one row per (s_ID, i_ID) pair — which instructor advises which student.
params.when_to_use: Querying which instructor(s) advise a given student or which students are advised by a given instructor. | Filtering or counting advisor relationships by student or instructor identifiers. | Composing with other views to add advisor identifiers to student- or instructor-level analyses, provided joins do not multiply rows per (s_ID, i_ID) pair without re-aggregation.
params.output_schema: s_ID: student identifier — derived directly from advisor.s_ID | i_ID: instructor identifier — derived directly from advisor.i_ID
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- implicit measure: count of advisor relationships (one row per s_ID,i_ID pair) | unique_students = COUNT(DISTINCT s_ID)  -- can be computed from the view | unique_instructors = COUNT(DISTINCT i_ID)  -- can be computed from the view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to student-level views (e.g., any view with primary key s_ID) on s_ID — safe because this view is at most one row per advisor relationship; joining to a student view that has exactly one row per s_ID will attach the advisor i_ID without duplicating student-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor-level views (e.g., any view with primary key i_ID) on i_ID — safe when the instructor view has one row per i_ID; this attaches student identifiers without duplicating instructor-level measures. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by s_ID or i_ID (for example, a enrollments table with multiple rows per s_ID or an instructor_publications table with multiple rows per i_ID) without first aggregating those tables to the same grain as advisor_rows (s_ID,i_ID) or to the join key's grain. Doing so will multiply advisor_rows' implicit measures (such as row_count) because multiple matched rows on the other side will produce multiple output rows per (s_ID,i_ID). | If you need counts or sums from a one-to-many child (e.g., number of enrollments per student) in the same result, either: (a) aggregate that child to one row per s_ID before joining on s_ID, or (b) aggregate after joining and GROUP BY the advisor_rows grain (s_ID, i_ID) to avoid double-counting. | Joining to other one-row-per-(s_ID,i_ID) views (or to normalized/joined views that preserve the same grain) is safe and will not duplicate measures, because keys match the same unique pair grain.

views.name: instructor_salary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor

params.description: Provides one-row-per-instructor basic attributes (ID, name, department name, salary).
params.when_to_use: Look up an instructor's name, department, or salary by ID or name. | Filter or join instructors as a dimension when computing aggregates (e.g., total payroll) after correct aggregation. | Serve as the canonical instructor row source when composing higher-level queries about instructors (headcount, average salary by department, etc.).
params.output_schema: ID: instructor.ID — unique identifier for the instructor (directly selected from the instructor table). | name: instructor.name — the instructor's full name (directly selected from the instructor table). | dept_name: instructor.dept_name — the name of the department the instructor belongs to (directly selected from the instructor table). | salary: instructor.salary — the instructor's salary amount (directly selected from the instructor table).
params.metric: salary = instructor.salary  -- atomic measure: numeric salary per instructor (no aggregation in this view).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_rows on department_rows.dept_name = instructor_salary.dept_name — safe because department_rows is one-row-per-department so joining will not duplicate instructor_salary rows; department-level aggregations can be computed by grouping instructor_salary after the join or by aggregating instructor_salary first. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_basic or department_with_courses_count on dept_name = dept_name — safe when those sibling views are one-row-per-department; they enrich department attributes without duplicating instructor measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_by_department on instructor_by_department.ID = instructor_salary.ID — safe if instructor_by_department is one-row-per-instructor (verify sibling view's grain) because it will not duplicate measures. | unsafe joins (will duplicate measures unless you re-aggregate): do NOT join instructor_salary directly to sections_with_classroom, sections_with_classroom_5, classroom_rows, classroom_rows_3, classrooms_by_building_cohort, or any sections/classroom-level views that are one-to-many with instructors without first aggregating those child rows. Those views are one-to-many relative to instructors (an instructor may teach multiple sections or be associated with multiple classroom rows), so a direct join would multiply instructor rows and inflate salary when you sum or average salaries. | If you need department-level totals (e.g., total payroll per department): either (a) aggregate instructor_salary by dept_name (SUM(salary) GROUP BY dept_name) or (b) join instructor_salary to a one-row-per-department view and then aggregate. Do not SUM(salary) after joining to a one-to-many child table without re-aggregation of the child side. | If combining with sections/classroom data to compute instructor-linked metrics (e.g., payroll per taught-section), first aggregate the many-side to one-row-per-instructor (e.g., count sections per instructor) and then join that result to instructor_salary on ID — this preserves salary as a one-row-per-instructor measure.

views.name: advisor_instructor_join

  advisor.i_ID AS i_ID,
  instructor.name AS instructor_name,
  instructor.dept_name AS instructor_dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS instructor_salary

JOIN instructor ON instructor.ID = advisor.i_ID

params.description: Pairs each student advisor assignment with the corresponding instructor's identifying info (name, department, salary).
params.when_to_use: Find the instructor (advisor) details for a given student ID or set of student IDs. | Filter or report on advisors by instructor attributes (e.g., department, salary) while keeping the student→advisor mapping. | Compose additional aggregations per instructor (e.g., count of advisees) by starting from student→instructor pairs. | Join instructor attributes onto student-level datasets where advisor i_ID is present.
params.output_schema: s_ID: student identifier from advisor.s_ID — the student who has an advisor (grain: one row per student-advisor pairing). | i_ID: instructor identifier from advisor.i_ID — the advisor's instructor ID (used as join key to instructor). | instructor_name: instructor.name — the instructor's full name as stored in the instructor table. | instructor_dept_name: instructor.dept_name — the department name for the instructor from the instructor table. | instructor_salary: instructor.salary — the instructor's salary value from the instructor table.
params.grounded_columns: advisor.s_ID | advisor.i_ID | instructor.ID | instructor.name | instructor.dept_name | instructor.salary
params.metric: No aggregated measures are produced by this view; all output columns are direct projections from base tables (no derived aggregates).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_by_department on i_ID = instructor_id — safe because this view is already one-row-per (s_ID, i_ID) and instructor_by_department should be one-row-per-instructor; joining will not duplicate advisor-level rows when instructor side is one-to-one. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_rows on instructor_dept_name = dept_name — safe only if department_rows is one-row-per-department; instructor_dept_name is a single value per row so measures are not duplicated when department is unique. | DO NOT join directly to any one-to-many child of instructor (for example: a hypothetical instructor_publications table with multiple rows per instructor) without aggregation — such a join would multiply advisor rows for instructors with multiple child rows and thus duplicate any measures derived from counting/aggregating advisees. Instead, first aggregate the many-side (e.g., count publications per instructor) into one-row-per-instructor, then join on i_ID. | DO NOT join to tables that are one-to-many with respect to s_ID (for example: a student_courses table with multiple course rows per student) if you intend to preserve one-row-per-advisor mapping; joining will replicate the advisor row for each matching student-side row. If you need aggregates at student level after such a join, aggregate back to s_ID (or s_ID+i_ID) before combining measures. | When composing higher-level aggregates per instructor (for example: number of advisees, average advisee GPA), aggregate this view grouped by i_ID (e.g., COUNT(s_ID) AS advisee_count) — because the view is at student→instructor grain, grouping by i_ID produces correct instructor-level metrics without duplication. | When composing instructor-level joins, prefer joining this view after aggregating to the desired grain (student-level, instructor-level) so downstream joins to one-to-many dimensions do not incorrectly multiply measures.

FROM teaches t

params.description: Provides the set of instructor-section assignments for fall-like semester rows (one row per teaches record), i.e., which instructor (ID) taught which course section (course_id, sec_id) in which semester and year.
params.when_to_use: List the sections taught by each instructor in a given semester/year. | Filter or join instructor assignments to other tables by course/section/semester/year. | Build aggregated instructor-level or course-level metrics by composing aggregation on top of these rows (e.g., count of sections taught per instructor in a term). | Serve as a grain-correct source when you need one row per teaches record to join to dimensions (instructor, course, section, semester) without duplicating teaching assignments.
params.output_schema: ID: instructor identifier — derived directly from teaches.ID | course_id: course identifier for the taught section — derived directly from teaches.course_id | sec_id: section identifier within the course for the taught section — derived directly from teaches.sec_id | semester: semester name/label for the taught section (e.g., 'Fall') — derived directly from teaches.semester | year: calendar year for the taught section — derived directly from teaches.year

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_by_department on ID = instructor_by_department.ID — safe because instructors_fall_teach_sections has one row per teaches record; joining to instructor_by_department (one row per instructor) will not duplicate measures if you subsequently aggregate by instructor, since instructor_by_department is 1:1 at instructor granularity. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_rows or department_basic only after joining instructor_by_department (instructor -> department) on department_id, or join on department key if you have pre-aggregated by department — join directly to department_rows on department_id is safe when you first reduce teaches rows to one row per department (re-aggregate) because department_rows is 1 row per department. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as sections_with_classroom or sections_with_classroom_5 without re-aggregation, because those views may expand a single teaches row into multiple rows when there are multiple classroom assignments or multiple matching section-classroom rows. Joining them directly would multiply teaches row counts and therefore inflate any measures derived from this view. | do NOT join directly to classroom_rows or classroom_rows_3 if they are many-to-one or many-to-many relative to a section (e.g., multiple classroom records per section) unless you first aggregate either side to the desired grain (for example, aggregate classroom capacity or count classrooms per section) to avoid duplicating teaches rows' contributions. | safe composition pattern: (a) use this view as the fact-level table (one row per teaching assignment); (b) join only to true dimension tables that are 1:1 at the join keys (e.g., instructor, course master by course_id if it is unique) without changing cardinality; (c) when joining to potential 1:N relationships (classrooms, meeting times, enrollments), perform aggregation on that relationship to the teaches grain (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) first, then join — this ensures measures computed from teaches are not multiplied. | example keys: join to department_via_instructor by ID -> instructor_by_department.ID (safe, 1:1 at instructor); join to department_with_courses_count only after grouping by department_id or joining via a deduplicated course dimension; to compute sections_per_instructor_by_year, aggregate this view by ID and year and then join to instructor or department dimensions.

views.name: course_basic_clean

FROM course

params.description: Provides one-row-per-course basic cleaned attributes (id, title, credits, department name).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve cleaned course metadata (title, credits, department) for a given course_id or set of course_ids. | Join course-level attributes into higher-level analyses (e.g., counts, aggregations) after safely accounting for cardinality. | Compose with department or classroom views to add course descriptive fields to those records.

params.metric: course_id = identity(course.course_id) | title = NULLIF(trim(course.title), '') | credits = CASE WHEN course.credits IS NOT NULL THEN course.credits ELSE NULL END | dept_name = NULLIF(trim(course.dept_name), '')
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_basic (or department_rows) on dept_name = department.dept_name — safe because department tables are keyed by department name (one department row per dept_name), so joining does NOT duplicate course rows (course grain remains one row per course). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_by_department on dept_name = instructor_by_department.dept_name — safe if instructor_by_department is one-row-per-department; verify that sibling view is not one-to-many before joining. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many section or classroom-level views (for example, sections_with_classroom, sections_with_classroom_5, classroom_rows, classroom_rows_3) without aggregation on the many-side first — those joins would multiply course rows because a single course.course_id can have multiple sections/classroom assignments, which would duplicate course-level attributes/metrics. | If you must combine with a one-to-many view (sections_with_classroom or classrooms_by_building_cohort), either: (a) pre-aggregate the many-side to one row per course.course_id (for example count of sections, distinct classroom count) and then join, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate grouping by course_id to restore one-row-per-course semantics. | When joining to department_with_courses_count (a JOIN/aggregate sibling), prefer joining on dept_name and be aware that that view likely contains a course-count metric; because course_basic_clean is one-row-per-course, joining to a per-department aggregate is safe (department is one row per department) but joining the reverse (adding course rows to a department-rows result) should be done with understanding of desired granularity. | Do not assume uniqueness of dept_name in the base course table; if department dimension in the database allows multiple rows per dept_name, confirm the dimension's uniqueness before declaring the join safe.

views.name: section_classroom_usage

  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  c.building,
  c.room_number,
  c.capacity

JOIN classroom AS c

  AND c.room_number IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides the classroom assignment and capacity for each course section (one row per section identified by course_id, sec_id, semester, year).

Such joins will duplicate section rows and therefore multiply any derived counts or sums. | Unsafe join example: do NOT join directly to a hypothetical section_meetings or enrollments view that has multiple rows per section without aggregating those rows to one row per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) first (e.g., aggregate to COUNT(meetings) or SUM(enrolled) and then join). | If you need to produce measures after joining to a many-side, re-aggregate using the original section grain: for example, to get total enrolled capacity utilization per section, first join enrollments aggregated to (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) then compute enrolled / capacity. | Key join signatures (safe because they are one-to-one or many-to-one from this view): join to classroom_rows ON (building, room_number); join to classroom_capacity_projection ON (building, room_number); join to sections_with_classroom or sections_with_classroom_5 only if you are aligning identical section grain keys — these are sibling JOIN views that should match one row per section. | Do not assume uniqueness when joining to AGG or NORM siblings unless their documented grain is compatible; always ensure the other view/table is one-row-per-(course_id, sec_id, semester, year) or aggregate it to that grain first.

views.name: courses_per_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS dept_course_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN
  course c
ON
  d.dept_name = c.dept_name
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name

params.description: For each department (dept_name), returns the number of courses assigned to that department (includes departments with zero courses).
params.when_to_use: Count of courses per department for reporting/dashboards | As a pre-aggregated input when joining department-level counts to other one-row-per-department entities (e.g., department budget or department metadata) | When composing higher-level metrics that need department course counts (e.g., average courses per department cohort) — use as a read-only aggregated building block | To detect departments with no courses (zero counts) because the view uses LEFT JOIN
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (sourced from department.dept_name) | dept_course_count: number of courses in that department (COUNT of course.course_id as produced by the view)
params.metric: dept_course_count = COUNT(course.course_id) -- an aggregate COUNT of course.course_id grouped by department.dept_name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department-level or one-row-per-department views/tables on department.dept_name — safe because courses_per_department is one-row-per-dept_name so its dept_course_count will not be duplicated. Example: join to department_budget_stats or department_basic on department.dept_name. | You may safely join to other normalized department views (e.g., department_rows, department_basic, department_name_length) on department.dept_name because those are expected to be one-row-per-department. | Do NOT directly join courses_per_department to any one-to-many detail table or view (for example: a sections table, a classrooms table if multiple classrooms relate to a department, or any JOIN that produces multiple rows per dept_name) without re-aggregation. Such joins would multiply dept_course_count and produce incorrect totals. Instead, either: |   - join to a one-row-per-department/table, or |   - aggregate the many-side first (produce one row per dept_name) and then join, or |   - join and then GROUP BY dept_name and re-aggregate measures (e.g., SUM(dept_course_count) would be incorrect unless you first deduplicate to one row per department). | Specific unsafe join examples: joining directly to sections_with_classroom, sections_with_classroom_5, classroom_rows, or classrooms_by_building_cohort (if any of those are one-to-many to department) without re-aggregation will duplicate counts. Instead join those views after reducing them to one row per dept_name or join courses_per_department into a query that groups by department.dept_name and recomputes COUNT(course.course_id) from the authoritative course table if needed.

views.name: prereq_relationships
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq

params.description: Lists prerequisite relationships between courses as one row per (course, prerequisite) pair.
params.when_to_use: Find all prerequisites for a given course_id or set of course_ids | Find all courses that require a given course as a prerequisite | Join prerequisites to course or department metadata to label courses or aggregate counts of prerequisite relationships | Compose into graphs of course dependency chains (as edges) or to count incoming/outgoing prerequisite edges per course
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the course that has a prerequisite — derives from prereq.course_id | prereq_id: identifier of the course that is required (the prerequisite) — derives from prereq.prereq_id
params.metric: course_id = prereq.course_id | prereq_id = prereq.prereq_id | Note: This view exposes no aggregated metrics; each row is a base-level relationship (edge) between two course IDs.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course-level dimension views (for example a course_basic or course_rows view) on course_id — safe because prereq_relationships is one-row-per (course_id, prereq_id) relationship and joining to a one-row-per-course dimension on course_id will not duplicate the meaning of each relationship row. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a course dimension on prereq_id to annotate the prerequisite course (e.g., join prereq_relationships.prereq_id = course_rows.course_id) — safe for the same reason: the dimension is one row per course. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables (for example, sections, enrollments, or any view that is one-to-many per course) on course_id or prereq_id without first aggregating those detail tables to one row per course. Doing a direct join to a table that has multiple rows per course would multiply the prereq_relationships rows and thus duplicate counts/metrics derived from this view. | If you need counts (e.g., number of prerequisites per course or number of courses that list a given course as a prerequisite), compute them by aggregating this view (e.g., GROUP BY course_id COUNT(*) AS num_prereqs) rather than by joining this view to a table with multiple rows per course. | When composing multi-step joins (for example: prereq_relationships -> course dimension -> department), ensure each intermediate join target is one-row-per-key (course or department). Joining to department should be done on department_id from the course dimension, not by joining prereq_relationships directly to department tables that are many-to-many relative to course rows.

views.name: course_with_prereq_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id,
  c.title,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM prereq p WHERE p.course_id = c.course_id
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_prereq
FROM course c

params.description: For each course, indicates its identifier, title, and whether that course has at least one prerequisite (binary flag).
params.when_to_use: When you need a per-course boolean flag indicating existence of any prerequisite (e.g., filter courses that require prerequisites). | As a dimension in reporting: combine with course attributes to segment courses by has_prereq = 0/1. | As a safe building block to join onto other course-level views or to aggregate counts of courses with/without prerequisites. | When composing additional course-level measures (counts, percentages) that must respect one-row-per-course grain.
params.output_schema: course_id: unique identifier for the course (from course.course_id) | title: course title (from course.title) | has_prereq: integer flag (1 or 0) indicating whether there exists at least one row in prereq with prereq.course_id = course.course_id; derived via CASE WHEN EXISTS subquery
params.metric: has_prereq = CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM prereq p WHERE p.course_id = course.course_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | note: has_prereq is a row-level boolean flag, not an aggregate. Aggregates over this column (SUM, AVG) produce course-counts or proportions and must be computed at the course grain or higher.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to course-level or one-row-per-course dimensions/views (for example 'department_with_courses_count' or other views keyed by course.course_id) on course_id — safe because course_with_prereq_flag has exactly one row per course.course_id, so its flag will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE: join to 'department_rows' or 'department_basic' only when joining through a single course->department key (i.e., course.course_id -> course.department_id -> department.*) provided the target is one-row-per-department; this keeps course rows distinct. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed to course.course_id that have multiple rows per course (for example: a hypothetical 'section' or 'classroom' view with multiple sections per course) without aggregation, because that will duplicate the course rows and thus duplicate the has_prereq flag in downstream sums. If you need course-level measures after such a join, first aggregate the many-side (e.g., COUNT(section_id) AS sections_per_course) grouped by course_id, then join back to this view on course_id. | If composing with sibling JOIN/NORM/AGG views that are many-to-one (e.g., sections_with_classroom which likely has multiple sections per course), either: |   - aggregate that sibling to one row per course (group by course_id) before joining, or |   - join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (explicitly GROUP BY course_id and use MAX(has_prereq) or MIN(has_prereq) to preserve the flag semantics). | When computing derived metrics across courses (e.g., number of courses with prerequisites per department), aggregate at the department level: SUM(has_prereq) grouped by department_id, joining course_with_prereq_flag to a department key that is one-row-per-department — do not join first to a many-sided view that expands courses.

params.metric: No derived numeric metrics in this view; it is a row-level projection. Example aggregate you can derive from it when composing: assignments_count = COUNT(*) grouped by chosen keys (e.g., instructor ID if joined first)

Such joins would multiply teaches_row_level rows and therefore multiply any counts or measures derived from teaches_row_level. | If you need to enrich teaches_row_level with many related rows (e.g., multiple classrooms, multiple enrollments), first aggregate those many-side tables to one row per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — the teaches_row_level grain — then join. Example safe pattern: LEFT JOIN (SELECT course_id, sec_id, semester, year, COUNT(*) AS enroll_count FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id, sec_id, semester, year) USING (course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | When composing aggregates: compute measures either by (A) aggregating teaches_row_level after joining only to one-row-per-key dimensions, or (B) by joining aggregated measures from many-side tables at the same grain (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) to avoid double counting. | Keys to prefer for joins: (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — these four columns define the view's grain and are the correct keys to join other datasets that are at section-instance level.

views.name: teaches_with_instructor

ON
